  1. nfd-topology-updater RBAC (#2564): the ClusterRole rule for noderesourcetopologies (API group topology.node.k8s.io) changes from create, get, update to create, patch. The Helm chart and the kustomize base ship the new rule, but a deployment that bumps only the image exits on its first NodeResourceTopology update with failed to apply NodeResourceTopology: noderesourcetopologies.topology.node.k8s.io "<node>" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<serviceaccount>" cannot patch resource "noderesourcetopologies" in API group "topology.node.k8s.io" at the cluster scope and crash-loops until the new ClusterRole is applied. The reverse also holds: a v0.19 topology-updater under the new ClusterRole is denied get on noderesourcetopologies, so pods still running v0.19 during the DaemonSet rollout, or after a rollback, fail until they run the matching version. If you manage RBAC outside the chart or kustomize, grant create, get, update and patch for the upgrade (and for any rollback), then drop get and update.
  2. nfd-topology-updater when the kubelet configuration is unavailable (#2564): previously a failed kubelet configuration read made nfd-topology-updater exit. Now it keeps the last cached configuration; if none was ever read, it skips the publish, logs skipping NodeResourceTopology publish, increments nfd_topology_updater_scan_errors_total and retries on the next event. With -oneshot it still exits with the error. Alerts that relied on topology-updater restarts should watch the metric instead.
  3. kustomize prune overlay (#2607): the prune Job now runs as its own nfd-prune ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding (get, list, patch, update on nodes and nodes/status), and the overlay no longer includes base/rbac. Applying or deleting the overlay no longer creates or deletes the nfd-master ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. The documented uninstall commands are unchanged.
  4. Full image base (#2632): the full image variant is based on debian:trixie-slim (Debian 13) instead of debian:bookworm-slim (Debian 12), which no longer publishes linux/s390x images. The NFD binaries are statically linked; anything you add on top of the full image now builds against Debian 13. The minimal image (scratch) is unchanged.
  5. nfd-topology-updater rollout pace (#2586): the Helm chart adds topologyUpdater.updateStrategy and sets rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: "10%", the same default as worker.updateStrategy. Upgrades now replace up to 10% of the topology-updater pods at a time instead of one (the Kubernetes DaemonSet default). Set topologyUpdater.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 1 to keep the old pace.

Fixes

  • nfd-gc: before deleting the NodeFeatures and NodeResourceTopology of a deleted Node, check the Node informer cache and keep the objects if a Node with that name exists again. nfd-gc can handle delete events minutes late after a mass Node deletion (client-go default 5 QPS); a Node re-created in that window lost its NodeFeature-derived labels and dropped out of NodeFeatureGroups until the publisher re-created its NodeFeatures (#2628).
  • Helm: pass gc.port to nfd-gc as -port. Previously nfd-gc always listened on 8080, so any other gc.port pointed the probes at a closed port and the pod crash-looped. With default values the only change is an added -port=8080 argument (#2608).
  • Helm: set metadata.namespace on the PodMonitor. When the chart is rendered through Kustomize's Helm integration (Kustomize 5.8 and later), the PodMonitor had no namespace and Argo CD refused to sync it with InvalidSpecError: Namespace for ... PodMonitor is missing (#2577, fixes #2576).
  • Helm: render priorityClassName once in the nfd-worker pod spec. With both the top-level priorityClassName and worker.priorityClassName set, the key was emitted twice and the effective value depended on the YAML decoder; worker.priorityClassName now takes precedence and falls back to the top-level value. The nfd-gc container securityContext is now configurable with gc.securityContext, which defaults to the previously hardcoded settings (#2624, fixes #2622).
  • kustomize: the prune overlay works again. It removed /rules/1 from the nfd-master ClusterRole with a JSON patch, and since v0.17.0 that index is the nodes rule, so the prune Job failed with nodes is forbidden: ... cannot list resource "nodes" and left all NFD labels, annotations and extended resources on the nodes (#2607).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroup status lists member nodes by Node name. It used the system.name feature's nodename element, so nodes whose features came only from third-party NodeFeature objects were listed with an empty name (#2621).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroups outside nfd-master's own namespace get their status populated. The update queue was keyed by object name only, so same-name NodeFeatureGroups in different namespaces collided, and the lookup and status write were pinned to nfd-master's namespace (#2559).
  • nfd-master: register the nfd_master_node_feature_group_update_requests_total counter. It was incremented but never registered, so it was missing from /metrics (#2625).
  • nfd compat validate-node: return the error when the registry referrers lookup fails (#2619), and fail on incomplete registry credential flags (--registry-username without --registry-password-stdin or --registry-token-stdin, or the reverse) instead of falling back to the default registry auth (#2620).

Documentation

  • Quick start, introduction and deployment guides: quick start commands and expected output, Helm parameter descriptions (regenerated chart README and values.schema.json; no default values changed), kustomize uninstall steps, metrics page, and a note that the OperatorHub NFD Operator is outdated (#2609).
  • Command line and configuration references for nfd-master, nfd-worker, nfd-topology-updater, nfd-gc and kubectl-nfd, compared flag by flag against the binaries' -help output; all klog flags documented (#2610).
  • API reference rendered with repository crd-ref-docs templates; scope, short names and status types of NodeFeature, NodeFeatureRule and NodeFeatureGroup documented; feature gates page and e2e configuration reference updated. The CRD manifests were regenerated with description-only changes: the schemas are unchanged, so no CRD re-apply is needed for this change (#2611).
  • Customization guide: NodeFeatureGroup, feature file and rule examples fixed and applied against a live cluster; the NodeFeatureGroup example is created in the nfd-master namespace so its status is populated (#2612).
  • Built-in feature label names and the image compatibility guide corrected (#2613).
  • Developer guide build and local-run commands fixed; contributing instructions point to the CNCF CLA (#2614).
  • Broken links and anchors fixed, the misspelled label domain in customization examples corrected, and -kubeconfig documented for nfd-topology-updater and nfd-gc (#2601).
  • Worker configuration reference: the sources.local section now states that the local source has no configuration options (#2605).
  • README rewritten with a components overview, Kubernetes version requirement, compatibility and community sections, and a nodeSelector example (#2623).
  • Helm chart: shorter worker.updateStrategy and topologyUpdater.updateStrategy descriptions, and the upgrade note on rolling-update pace now covers nfd-topology-updater (#2635).
  • README and the netlify redirect point to v0.19 (#2557).

Dependencies

  • Go 1.26 -> 1.27, builder image golang:1.26-trixie -> golang:1.27-trixie (#2583).
  • Kubernetes libraries v0.35.3 -> v0.37.1, including k8s.io/kubernetes v1.35.3 -> v1.37.1 and the replace pins (#2584). The PR changes only go.mod, go.sum and the podresources client call signature; no manifest or API version changes.
  • github.com/k8stopologyawareschedwg/noderesourcetopology-api 0.1.2 -> 0.1.4 (#2564, #2592).

title: Do not panic when stopping an MPS daemon that did not finish starting
body: ## Description If `Daemon.Start` fails after `nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d` has run (for example a pinned memory limit command fails), `startDaemons` returns `restartDaemons=true` and `start` calls `Stop` on every daemon before retrying. Once `quit` succeeds, `Stop` calls [`d.logTailer.Stop()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin/blob/1053da35d5a67fdbc3f0ea0877b7178026048769/cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/daemon.go#L168-L169) on a log tailer that `Start` only creates at its end, so `mps-control-daemon` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` instead of retrying. This has been so since v0.15.0-rc.2. The [`os.Remove` error is compared with `!= os.ErrNotExist`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin/blob/1053da35d5a67fdbc3f0ea0877b7178026048769/cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/daemon.go#L175-L177), which a `*PathError` never equals, so the missing started file comes back as `failed to remove started file: ...: no such file or directory` and `start` exits with `error stopping plugins from previous run`. `Stop` now only stops a log tailer that exists, and uses `errors.Is`. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`golangci-lint run ./cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/...`, 0 issues) - [x] Unit tests passing (`go test ./cmd/mps-control-daemon/...`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (no dependency changes) - [x] Third-party notices in-sync (no dependency changes) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing `TestDaemonStop` puts a stand-in `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` on the `PATH`. `go test -count=3 -run TestDaemonStop ./cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/` fails on main with the nil pointer dereference and passes with this change. Reverting either hunk alone makes it fail. ---

title: [Bug]: MPS replicas above 16 are rejected on Volta GPUs (compute capability 7.0 and 7.2)
body:
### 1. Quick Debug Information
* OS/Version, kernel, container runtime, K8s flavor: not run on a cluster; found by reading the code and confirmed with the unit tests in `cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps` on main (1053da35d) with Go 1.27.2 on macOS arm64.
* Affected versions: the check is unchanged since #593 and is in v0.20.1.

### 2. Issue or feature description

#593 limits MPS replicas to "48 on Volta or newer systems, 16 on older systems". The check compares the device compute capability with 7.5:

```go
// cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/device.go
func (d *mpsDevice) isAtLeastVolta() bool {
	vCc := "v" + strings.TrimPrefix(d.ComputeCapability, "v")
	return semver.Compare(semver.Canonical(vCc), semver.Canonical("v7.5")) >= 0
}
```

7.5 is Turing. Volta is 7.0 (V100, TITAN V) and 7.2 (Jetson AGX Xavier), so on Volta `maxClients()` returns 16 instead of 48. The existing test cases in `device_test.go` label compute capability 7.0 as "pre-volta", which matches the code but not the intent of #593.

Current behaviour: with `sharing.mps.resources[].replicas` between 17 and 48 on a V100 or Xavier node, `assertReplicas` fails with `invalid device maximum allowed replicas exceeded: N > 16`, so the MPS control daemon does not start and the shared resource is not advertised.

Expected behaviour: Volta devices accept up to 48 replicas, as on Turing and newer.

For reference, the current MPS documentation gives a general limit of 60 client CUDA contexts per device with the default `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, so the 48 itself may be worth a separate look. This issue is only about where the Volta boundary sits.

A fix that compares with 7.0 and moves the pre-Volta test cases to compute capability 6.1 is in #2117.

title: Allow 48 MPS clients on Volta devices
body: ## Description `isAtLeastVolta` compared the compute capability with 7.5 (Turing), so Volta devices (7.0 and 7.2) were held to the pre-Volta limit of 16 MPS clients, and MPS replicas above 16 were rejected on V100 and Xavier nodes. #593 meant the limit to be 48 on Volta or newer. The comparison now uses 7.0. The test cases that called compute capability 7.0 "pre-volta" now use 6.1 (Pascal), and two cases cover 7.0 and 7.2 at 48 clients. Closes #2116 ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) (ran `golangci-lint run ./cmd/mps-control-daemon/mps/...`: 0 issues) - [x] Unit tests passing (`make test`) (ran `go test ./cmd/mps-control-daemon/...`) - [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make check-modules`) (not run; no dependency changes) - [ ] Third-party notices in-sync (`make check-third-party-notices`) (not run; no dependency changes) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing `TestDevice` with the new Volta cases fails on main (both report 16 clients) and passes with this change. Go 1.27.2, macOS arm64. Not tested on a Volta GPU node. ---

title: Add health-checking via gpu recovery actions API
body:
## Description

This PR allows the device-plugin to dynamically derive health status from the GPU recovery actions API, with the existing XID-based approach preserved as a fallback. The main advantages of this approach are 1) GPUs can be recovered from the unhealthy state, and 2) unhealthy criteria is richer (than XID allowlist) with its responsibility is offloaded to the NVML team. 

Closes [#552](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/552)

title: Bump github/codeql-action from 4.37.4 to 4.39.1
body:
Bumps [github/codeql-action](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.37.4 to 4.39.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

v4.38.1

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

v4.38.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

title: Label compute capability 11.x GPUs as the blackwell family
body: ## Description Jetson Thor modules (Jetson T5000 and T4000) report CUDA compute capability 11.0, according to https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus. `getArchFamily` only maps majors 10 and 12 to `blackwell`, so on these devices GFD sets `nvidia.com/gpu.family=undefined`, while `gpu.compute.major` is `11`. This PR adds 11 to the blackwell case and updates the comment that said the family only covers 10.0 and 12.0. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) (golangci-lint is not installed locally; `gofmt -l` and `go vet ./internal/lm/` are clean) - [x] Unit tests passing (`make test`) (ran `go test ./...`, all pass) - [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make check-modules`) (not run; the change does not touch go.mod or vendor) - [ ] Third-party notices in-sync (`make check-third-party-notices`) (not run; no dependency changes) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Added `TestGetArchFamily` in `internal/lm/resource_test.go` with the Blackwell compute capabilities 10.0, 10.3, 11.0, 12.0 and 12.1. On main the 11.0 case fails (`expected: "blackwell"`, `actual: "undefined"`). With this change all cases pass. I did not test on Thor hardware. ---

title: build(deps): bump sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery/api/nfd from 0.19.0 to 0.20.1
body:
Bumps [sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery/api/nfd](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-feature-discovery) from 0.19.0 to 0.20.1.
Release notes

Sourced from sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery/api/nfd's releases.

v0.20.1

NFD v0.20.1 is a maintenance release for the v0.20 series.

  • Build with Go 1.27.3. This includes the crypto/x509 fix for GO-2026-6809 / CVE-2026-111943. Certificate verification rejects known untrusted intermediate certificates. #2646
  • Update deployment images, chart application version, documentation, and installation commands to v0.20.1. #2647

There are no public API changes.

Install the Helm chart:

helm install -n node-feature-discovery --create-namespace nfd \
  oci://registry.k8s.io/nfd/charts/node-feature-discovery --version 0.20.1

Full comparison

v0.20.0

Highlights

  • nfd-topology-updater writes NodeResourceTopology objects with server-side apply (field manager node-feature-discovery-topology-updater, forced) instead of a GET followed by an UPDATE: one API request per update instead of two, which lowers kube-apiserver and etcd load at scale (#2564). Requires an RBAC update, see Action Required.
  • nfd-topology-updater caches the kubelet configuration and CPU core attributes and refreshes them on interval-based scans. Reads from the kubelet configz endpoint now time out after 2 minutes (previously no timeout), and a failed read no longer stops the process (#2564). See Action Required.
  • Built with Go 1.27: go.mod declares go 1.27 and the builder image is golang:1.27-trixie (#2583).
  • Built against the Kubernetes v1.37 libraries: k8s.io/* v0.35.3 -> v0.37.1, k8s.io/kubernetes v1.35.3 -> v1.37.1 (#2584).
  • nfd-gc no longer deletes the NodeFeatures and NodeResourceTopology of a Node that was deleted and created again with the same name before nfd-gc handled the delete event (#2628).
  • Documentation pass: the quick start, deployment, usage, reference and developer guide pages were re-checked against a live deployment of master (Helm chart and kustomize overlays) and corrected (#2601, #2605, #2609, #2610, #2611, #2612, #2613, #2614).

Action Required / Behavior Changes

  1. nfd-topology-updater RBAC (#2564): the ClusterRole rule for noderesourcetopologies (API group topology.node.k8s.io) changes from create, get, update to create, patch. The Helm chart and the kustomize base ship the new rule, but a deployment that bumps only the image exits on its first NodeResourceTopology update with failed to apply NodeResourceTopology: noderesourcetopologies.topology.node.k8s.io "<node>" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<serviceaccount>" cannot patch resource "noderesourcetopologies" in API group "topology.node.k8s.io" at the cluster scope and crash-loops until the new ClusterRole is applied. The reverse also holds: a v0.19 topology-updater under the new ClusterRole is denied get on noderesourcetopologies, so pods still running v0.19 during the DaemonSet rollout, or after a rollback, fail until they run the matching version. If you manage RBAC outside the chart or kustomize, grant create, get, update and patch for the upgrade (and for any rollback), then drop get and update.
  2. nfd-topology-updater when the kubelet configuration is unavailable (#2564): previously a failed kubelet configuration read made nfd-topology-updater exit. Now it keeps the last cached configuration; if none was ever read, it skips the publish, logs skipping NodeResourceTopology publish, increments nfd_topology_updater_scan_errors_total and retries on the next event. With -oneshot it still exits with the error. Alerts that relied on topology-updater restarts should watch the metric instead.
  3. kustomize prune overlay (#2607): the prune Job now runs as its own nfd-prune ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding (get, list, patch, update on nodes and nodes/status), and the overlay no longer includes base/rbac. Applying or deleting the overlay no longer creates or deletes the nfd-master ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. The documented uninstall commands are unchanged.
  4. Full image base (#2632): the full image variant is based on debian:trixie-slim (Debian 13) instead of debian:bookworm-slim (Debian 12), which no longer publishes linux/s390x images. The NFD binaries are statically linked; anything you add on top of the full image now builds against Debian 13. The minimal image (scratch) is unchanged.
  5. nfd-topology-updater rollout pace (#2586): the Helm chart adds topologyUpdater.updateStrategy and sets rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: "10%", the same default as worker.updateStrategy. Upgrades now replace up to 10% of the topology-updater pods at a time instead of one (the Kubernetes DaemonSet default). Set topologyUpdater.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 1 to keep the old pace.

Fixes

  • nfd-gc: before deleting the NodeFeatures and NodeResourceTopology of a deleted Node, check the Node informer cache and keep the objects if a Node with that name exists again. nfd-gc can handle delete events minutes late after a mass Node deletion (client-go default 5 QPS); a Node re-created in that window lost its NodeFeature-derived labels and dropped out of NodeFeatureGroups until the publisher re-created its NodeFeatures (#2628).
  • Helm: pass gc.port to nfd-gc as -port. Previously nfd-gc always listened on 8080, so any other gc.port pointed the probes at a closed port and the pod crash-looped. With default values the only change is an added -port=8080 argument (#2608).
  • Helm: set metadata.namespace on the PodMonitor. When the chart is rendered through Kustomize's Helm integration (Kustomize 5.8 and later), the PodMonitor had no namespace and Argo CD refused to sync it with InvalidSpecError: Namespace for ... PodMonitor is missing (#2577, fixes #2576).
  • Helm: render priorityClassName once in the nfd-worker pod spec. With both the top-level priorityClassName and worker.priorityClassName set, the key was emitted twice and the effective value depended on the YAML decoder; worker.priorityClassName now takes precedence and falls back to the top-level value. The nfd-gc container securityContext is now configurable with gc.securityContext, which defaults to the previously hardcoded settings (#2624, fixes #2622).
  • kustomize: the prune overlay works again. It removed /rules/1 from the nfd-master ClusterRole with a JSON patch, and since v0.17.0 that index is the nodes rule, so the prune Job failed with nodes is forbidden: ... cannot list resource "nodes" and left all NFD labels, annotations and extended resources on the nodes (#2607).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroup status lists member nodes by Node name. It used the system.name feature's nodename element, so nodes whose features came only from third-party NodeFeature objects were listed with an empty name (#2621).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroups outside nfd-master's own namespace get their status populated. The update queue was keyed by object name only, so same-name NodeFeatureGroups in different namespaces collided, and the lookup and status write were pinned to nfd-master's namespace (#2559).
  • nfd-master: register the nfd_master_node_feature_group_update_requests_total counter. It was incremented but never registered, so it was missing from /metrics (#2625).
  • nfd compat validate-node: return the error when the registry referrers lookup fails (#2619), and fail on incomplete registry credential flags (--registry-username without --registry-password-stdin or --registry-token-stdin, or the reverse) instead of falling back to the default registry auth (#2620).

Documentation

  • Quick start, introduction and deployment guides: quick start commands and expected output, Helm parameter descriptions (regenerated chart README and values.schema.json; no default values changed), kustomize uninstall steps, metrics page, and a note that the OperatorHub NFD Operator is outdated (#2609).
  • Command line and configuration references for nfd-master, nfd-worker, nfd-topology-updater, nfd-gc and kubectl-nfd, compared flag by flag against the binaries' -help output; all klog flags documented (#2610).
  • API reference rendered with repository crd-ref-docs templates; scope, short names and status types of NodeFeature, NodeFeatureRule and NodeFeatureGroup documented; feature gates page and e2e configuration reference updated. The CRD manifests were regenerated with description-only changes: the schemas are unchanged, so no CRD re-apply is needed for this change (#2611).
  • Customization guide: NodeFeatureGroup, feature file and rule examples fixed and applied against a live cluster; the NodeFeatureGroup example is created in the nfd-master namespace so its status is populated (#2612).
  • Built-in feature label names and the image compatibility guide corrected (#2613).

... (truncated)

title: build(deps): bump google.golang.org/grpc from 1.83.2 to 1.85.0
body:
Bumps [google.golang.org/grpc](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go) from 1.83.2 to 1.85.0.
Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.85.0

New Features

  • stats: Expose the effective client authority (sent on the wire as the HTTP/2 :authority header) in client stats.OutHeader events. (#9296)
    • Special Thanks: @​aryansk
  • metadata: Add ValueFromOutgoingContext, which reads a single metadata value from outgoing context without copying the entire outgoing metadata into a new map. (#9282)
    • Special Thanks: @​yuyangguo42

Bug Fixes

  • transport: Refine control buffer throttling to only count peer-induced control frames, raise the default GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT from 100 to 10,000, and close client connections if reads remain throttled for 10s. (#9563)
  • server: Ensure Stop() forcefully terminates the server while GracefulStop() is waiting for active handlers to complete. (#9394)
    • Special Thanks: @​stanhu
  • server: Unconditionally increment the highest-seen stream ID on when handling HEADERS frames to comply with RFC 7540 §5.1.1. Previously, truncated HEADERS frames left the connection in an inconsistent state and allowed stream IDs to be reused by clients without resulting in a protocol error. (#9414)
  • server: Terminate streams immediately when a HEADERS frame includes the EndStream bit. Previously, this caused server handlers to hang when reading a message. (#9391)
  • server: Reject requests missing both :authority and Host headers with HTTP 400 and status Internal. (#9365)
  • xds: Fix a bug where route header matchers with non-lowercase names failed to match routes. (#9353)
    • Special Thanks: @​winklemad
  • client: Ensure retried RPCs use the correct :authority value specified by the LB policy instead of inheriting it from a previous attempt. (#9277)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • transport: Fail streams with io.ErrUnexpectedEOF instead of io.EOF upon receiving truncated message headers or bodies after partial data has already been received. (#9204)
    • Special Thanks: @​buger

Release 1.84.0

Behavior Changes

  • stats/otel: The grpc.lb.pick_first.* metrics have been removed and replaced with grpc.subchannel.* metrics. See gRFC A94 for more details. (#9215)

New Features

  • xds: Add support for contains_match in route header matchers. (#9223)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug

Bug Fixes

  • client: Fix a bug where a ClientConn could get permanently stuck in IDLE when an RPC was canceled during stream creation. Previously, such cancellations triggered stream cleanup twice, corrupting the channel's idleness state and causing subsequent RPCs to fail with deadline exceeded errors. (#9191)
    • Special Thanks: @​utkuozdemir
  • client: Fix a bug where non-gRPC HTTP responses ending with an empty DATA frame failed the RPC with status code Internal instead of preserving the HTTP-mapped status code and response body. (#9217)
    • Special Thanks: @​chengxilo
  • credentials: Validate metadata returned by per-RPC credentials, failing the RPC with status code Internal if invalid keys or values are found. Previously, invalid metadata from credentials was sent to the server in outgoing HTTP/2 requests. (#9202)
    • Special Thanks: @​buger
  • credentials/sts: Prevent potential token leakage by disallowing HTTP redirects during STS token exchange. Previously, 3xx redirects were followed automatically, replaying the request body containing authentication tokens to the redirect destination. (#9299)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • randomsubsetting: Ignore endpoints that contain no addresses. Previously, this could cause the policy to panic while computing hashes. (#9259)
    • Special Thanks: @​fallintoplace
  • stats/otel: Ensure method names are populated in trace spans when metrics are disabled. Previously, running with tracing enabled and metrics disabled resulted in server trace spans lacking the RPC method name (recording only "Recv."). (#9262)
  • transport: Return io.ErrUnexpectedEOF when EOF is encountered after partial header or message body reads. Previously, partial reads could return a plain io.EOF, failing to distinguish truncated data from a clean end of stream. (#9204)
    • Special Thanks: @​buger
  • transport: Validate metadata supplied by balancers (in PickResult.Metadata) and resolver addresses, failing the RPC with status code Internal if invalid keys or values are found. Previously, invalid metadata from these sources was sent to the server in outgoing HTTP/2 requests. (#9203)
    • Special Thanks: @​buger

title: build(deps): bump sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery from 0.19.0 to 0.20.1
body:
Bumps [sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-feature-discovery) from 0.19.0 to 0.20.1.
Release notes

Sourced from sigs.k8s.io/node-feature-discovery's releases.

v0.20.1

NFD v0.20.1 is a maintenance release for the v0.20 series.

  • Build with Go 1.27.3. This includes the crypto/x509 fix for GO-2026-6809 / CVE-2026-111943. Certificate verification rejects known untrusted intermediate certificates. #2646
  • Update deployment images, chart application version, documentation, and installation commands to v0.20.1. #2647

There are no public API changes.

Install the Helm chart:

helm install -n node-feature-discovery --create-namespace nfd \
  oci://registry.k8s.io/nfd/charts/node-feature-discovery --version 0.20.1

Full comparison

v0.20.0

Highlights

  • nfd-topology-updater writes NodeResourceTopology objects with server-side apply (field manager node-feature-discovery-topology-updater, forced) instead of a GET followed by an UPDATE: one API request per update instead of two, which lowers kube-apiserver and etcd load at scale (#2564). Requires an RBAC update, see Action Required.
  • nfd-topology-updater caches the kubelet configuration and CPU core attributes and refreshes them on interval-based scans. Reads from the kubelet configz endpoint now time out after 2 minutes (previously no timeout), and a failed read no longer stops the process (#2564). See Action Required.
  • Built with Go 1.27: go.mod declares go 1.27 and the builder image is golang:1.27-trixie (#2583).
  • Built against the Kubernetes v1.37 libraries: k8s.io/* v0.35.3 -> v0.37.1, k8s.io/kubernetes v1.35.3 -> v1.37.1 (#2584).
  • nfd-gc no longer deletes the NodeFeatures and NodeResourceTopology of a Node that was deleted and created again with the same name before nfd-gc handled the delete event (#2628).
  • Documentation pass: the quick start, deployment, usage, reference and developer guide pages were re-checked against a live deployment of master (Helm chart and kustomize overlays) and corrected (#2601, #2605, #2609, #2610, #2611, #2612, #2613, #2614).

Action Required / Behavior Changes

  1. nfd-topology-updater RBAC (#2564): the ClusterRole rule for noderesourcetopologies (API group topology.node.k8s.io) changes from create, get, update to create, patch. The Helm chart and the kustomize base ship the new rule, but a deployment that bumps only the image exits on its first NodeResourceTopology update with failed to apply NodeResourceTopology: noderesourcetopologies.topology.node.k8s.io "<node>" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<serviceaccount>" cannot patch resource "noderesourcetopologies" in API group "topology.node.k8s.io" at the cluster scope and crash-loops until the new ClusterRole is applied. The reverse also holds: a v0.19 topology-updater under the new ClusterRole is denied get on noderesourcetopologies, so pods still running v0.19 during the DaemonSet rollout, or after a rollback, fail until they run the matching version. If you manage RBAC outside the chart or kustomize, grant create, get, update and patch for the upgrade (and for any rollback), then drop get and update.
  2. nfd-topology-updater when the kubelet configuration is unavailable (#2564): previously a failed kubelet configuration read made nfd-topology-updater exit. Now it keeps the last cached configuration; if none was ever read, it skips the publish, logs skipping NodeResourceTopology publish, increments nfd_topology_updater_scan_errors_total and retries on the next event. With -oneshot it still exits with the error. Alerts that relied on topology-updater restarts should watch the metric instead.
  3. kustomize prune overlay (#2607): the prune Job now runs as its own nfd-prune ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding (get, list, patch, update on nodes and nodes/status), and the overlay no longer includes base/rbac. Applying or deleting the overlay no longer creates or deletes the nfd-master ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. The documented uninstall commands are unchanged.
  4. Full image base (#2632): the full image variant is based on debian:trixie-slim (Debian 13) instead of debian:bookworm-slim (Debian 12), which no longer publishes linux/s390x images. The NFD binaries are statically linked; anything you add on top of the full image now builds against Debian 13. The minimal image (scratch) is unchanged.
  5. nfd-topology-updater rollout pace (#2586): the Helm chart adds topologyUpdater.updateStrategy and sets rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: "10%", the same default as worker.updateStrategy. Upgrades now replace up to 10% of the topology-updater pods at a time instead of one (the Kubernetes DaemonSet default). Set topologyUpdater.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 1 to keep the old pace.

Fixes

  • nfd-gc: before deleting the NodeFeatures and NodeResourceTopology of a deleted Node, check the Node informer cache and keep the objects if a Node with that name exists again. nfd-gc can handle delete events minutes late after a mass Node deletion (client-go default 5 QPS); a Node re-created in that window lost its NodeFeature-derived labels and dropped out of NodeFeatureGroups until the publisher re-created its NodeFeatures (#2628).
  • Helm: pass gc.port to nfd-gc as -port. Previously nfd-gc always listened on 8080, so any other gc.port pointed the probes at a closed port and the pod crash-looped. With default values the only change is an added -port=8080 argument (#2608).
  • Helm: set metadata.namespace on the PodMonitor. When the chart is rendered through Kustomize's Helm integration (Kustomize 5.8 and later), the PodMonitor had no namespace and Argo CD refused to sync it with InvalidSpecError: Namespace for ... PodMonitor is missing (#2577, fixes #2576).
  • Helm: render priorityClassName once in the nfd-worker pod spec. With both the top-level priorityClassName and worker.priorityClassName set, the key was emitted twice and the effective value depended on the YAML decoder; worker.priorityClassName now takes precedence and falls back to the top-level value. The nfd-gc container securityContext is now configurable with gc.securityContext, which defaults to the previously hardcoded settings (#2624, fixes #2622).
  • kustomize: the prune overlay works again. It removed /rules/1 from the nfd-master ClusterRole with a JSON patch, and since v0.17.0 that index is the nodes rule, so the prune Job failed with nodes is forbidden: ... cannot list resource "nodes" and left all NFD labels, annotations and extended resources on the nodes (#2607).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroup status lists member nodes by Node name. It used the system.name feature's nodename element, so nodes whose features came only from third-party NodeFeature objects were listed with an empty name (#2621).
  • nfd-master: NodeFeatureGroups outside nfd-master's own namespace get their status populated. The update queue was keyed by object name only, so same-name NodeFeatureGroups in different namespaces collided, and the lookup and status write were pinned to nfd-master's namespace (#2559).
  • nfd-master: register the nfd_master_node_feature_group_update_requests_total counter. It was incremented but never registered, so it was missing from /metrics (#2625).
  • nfd compat validate-node: return the error when the registry referrers lookup fails (#2619), and fail on incomplete registry credential flags (--registry-username without --registry-password-stdin or --registry-token-stdin, or the reverse) instead of falling back to the default registry auth (#2620).

Documentation

  • Quick start, introduction and deployment guides: quick start commands and expected output, Helm parameter descriptions (regenerated chart README and values.schema.json; no default values changed), kustomize uninstall steps, metrics page, and a note that the OperatorHub NFD Operator is outdated (#2609).
  • Command line and configuration references for nfd-master, nfd-worker, nfd-topology-updater, nfd-gc and kubectl-nfd, compared flag by flag against the binaries' -help output; all klog flags documented (#2610).
  • API reference rendered with repository crd-ref-docs templates; scope, short names and status types of NodeFeature, NodeFeatureRule and NodeFeatureGroup documented; feature gates page and e2e configuration reference updated. The CRD manifests were regenerated with description-only changes: the schemas are unchanged, so no CRD re-apply is needed for this change (#2611).
  • Customization guide: NodeFeatureGroup, feature file and rule examples fixed and applied against a live cluster; the NodeFeatureGroup example is created in the nfd-master namespace so its status is populated (#2612).
  • Built-in feature label names and the image compatibility guide corrected (#2613).

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 848df70 Merge pull request #2647 from faganihajizada/chore/release-v0.20.1
  • 2cfedf7 Merge pull request #2646 from faganihajizada/chore/prepare-v0.20.1
  • 49061a8 Release v0.20.1
  • fc554c4 build: bump Go to v1.27.3
  • 469c89e Merge pull request #2637 from ArangoGutierrez/chore/prepare-v0.20.0
  • 3e6d6f1 Release v0.20.0
  • 94e107b Merge pull request #2635 from ArangoGutierrez/docs/2523-updatestrategy-descri...
  • 680a6c5 docs(helm): cover the topology-updater in the rolling-update upgrade note
  • 46f47ce docs(helm): shorten the updateStrategy descriptions
  • 22a072c Merge pull request #2586 from shashankvarma499/topologyupdater-updatestrategy
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

[v0.5.1] - 2026-10-25

[v0.5.0] - 2026-10-13

Features

  • feat(aws): optional availabilityZone on instance and cluster specs (#878, @​abrarshivani): Pins every subnet and node to one zone of the region. The pre-flight rejects a pinned zone that does not offer the requested instance types and lists the zones that do.

Bug Fixes

  • fix(aws): create subnets in an availability zone that offers the instance types (#878, @​abrarshivani): Subnets were created without an Availability Zone, so AWS could place them in a zone that does not offer the instance type (for example g5g.xlarge in us-west-2d). RunInstances then failed after the VPC existed, and the rollback could leak the VPC. The pre-flight now uses DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings to pick a standard zone that offers every instance type the environment needs, and Create(), CreateCluster() and DryRun() fail before anything is created when no zone does. title: Fix broken GPU allocation for devices with NVML_ERROR_RESET_REQUIRED
body:
## Description

Closes #[625](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/625)

GPU allocation via `alignedAlloc` specifically can fail when a device on the affected node has status `NVML_ERROR_RESET_REQUIRED`. 

This is because `alignedAlloc` calls a `go-gpuallocator` method (`gpuallocator.NewDevices`) that attempts to acquire an NVML handle and query each GPU on the node through calling `go-nvml`'s `GetDevices`. The problem is that if any of the GPUs on said node have the error `NVML_ERROR_RESET_REQUIRED`, acquiring the handle & querying them fails, causing the allocate method to fail and no workloads to schedule with GPUs. 

Even one errored out GPU can cause allocation for all GPUs on the same node to fail. This fix still results in the first GPU allocation failing with this error, but subsequent allocations do not fail. 

The solution to this is two-part: 
1) Make `alignedAlloc` only query the healthy list of devices. Currently, it queries all GPUs and then filters the list according to healthy GPUs. 
2) Send unhealthy GPUs reported during querying to the Unhealthy channel so that future allocations work. 

To avoid updating `go-gpuallocator`, the following workaround was implemented: 
Before: `gpuallocator.NewDevices` used `go-nvlib`'s default device library, which gets a handle for every GPU on the node by index.
Now: Added `requestedDeviceLib`, a wrapper around the standard GPU-listing library (go-nvlib). It redefines `GetDevices` to only get handles for healthy GPUs. 

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes
- [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`)
- [x] Unit tests passing (`make test`)
- [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make check-modules`)
- [x] Test cases are added for new code paths

## Testing

Unit tests added. Manual testing was also done on a node: `NVML_ERROR_RESET_REQUIRED` was injected upon NVML handle lookup (without an XID). The affected GPU (L40) was reported as unhealthy. Node GPU capacity stayed at 2 while allocatable dropped to 1. Subsequent `GetPreferredAllocation` calls to the second GPU on that node succeeded.

title: [Bug]: Helm chart adds SYS_ADMIN and MIG monitor devices for any embedded config.map
body:
### 1. Quick Debug Information
* Helm chart: `deployments/helm/nvidia-device-plugin` on main (also in v0.20.x). Found with `helm template`, no cluster needed.

### 2. Issue or feature description

When the chart builds the ConfigMap from `config.map`, the device plugin and config-manager containers always get `capabilities.add: [SYS_ADMIN]` and `NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES=all`, even when no config in the map uses a MIG strategy or the `volume-mounts` device list strategy. GFD and the MPS control daemon use the same helpers. The common time-slicing setup is affected:

```yaml
config:
  map:
    default: |-
      version: v1
      flags:
        migStrategy: none
      sharing:
        timeSlicing:
          resources:
          - name: nvidia.com/gpu
            replicas: 4
```

```
$ helm template ndp deployments/helm/nvidia-device-plugin -n gpu -f values.yaml -s templates/daemonset-device-plugin.yml | grep -c SYS_ADMIN
2
```

Cause: `allPossibleMigStrategiesAreNone` and `deviceListStrategyIncludesVolumeMount` in `_helpers.tpl` check `hasConfigMap` before looking at `config.map`. `hasConfigMap` is true for an embedded map as well as for an external `config.name`, so the branch that reads the embedded configs is never reached. That branch also has two problems of its own once reached: a config with `flags` but no `migStrategy` counts as MIG (the plugin defaults to `none`), and `typeIs "list"` never matches a list from `fromYaml`, and each config overwrites the result of the previous one.

Expected: with an embedded map, SYS_ADMIN and the MIG monitor devices are added only if some config needs them. With an external `config.name` the contents are unknown, so keeping them there is fine.

Same report as #854, which was closed by the stale bot without a fix. I have a fix with tests in `tests/helm` and will open a PR.

title: Inspect embedded config.map entries before adding SYS_ADMIN
body: ## Description With an embedded `config.map`, the chart gives the device plugin and config-manager containers `SYS_ADMIN` and sets `NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES=all`, even when no config uses a MIG strategy or `volume-mounts`. A plain time-slicing config is enough to trigger it. GFD and the MPS control daemon use the same helpers. `allPossibleMigStrategiesAreNone` and `deviceListStrategyIncludesVolumeMount` returned early on `hasConfigMap`, which is true for an embedded map too, so the loop over `config.map` was never reached. The early return now applies only to an external `config.name`, whose contents the chart can't see. The loop itself is also fixed: a missing `migStrategy` counts as `none` (the plugin default), a `deviceListStrategy` list is matched with `kindIs "slice"` (`typeIs "list"` never matched), and once one config needs the capability, later configs no longer reset it. Null `flags`/`plugin` values are handled. Closes #2154 ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [ ] Unit tests passing (`make test`) - [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make check-modules`) - [ ] Third-party notices in-sync (`make check-third-party-notices`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing `TestDevicePluginDaemonsetEmbeddedConfigCapabilities` in `tests/helm` covers time-slicing only, configs without flags, empty `flags.plugin`, one MIG config, one `volume-mounts` list, and an external `config.name`. Four of the six cases fail on main. `cd tests/helm && go test ./...` passes (101 tests). No Go code outside `tests/helm` changed, so I didn't run `make lint`/`make test`. This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. ---

Performance

  • aws: skip the guest OS shutdown when terminating EC2 instances (#922, @​tariq1890): holodeck delete, holodeck cleanup and the GitHub Action's VPC cleanup now terminate instances with SkipOsShutdown. Terminations took over 7 minutes before this change.

Releases now build with the Dockerfile's Go, the same as CI, and the Dockerfile moves to golang:1.27.3-bookworm.

Bug Fixes

  • CI: golangci-lint 2.15.0 and ubuntu-26.04 runner fixes (#908, #909): An unchecked error in a pkg/sshutil test now fails the test with the error message. The docs-check job pins Ruby 4.0, because '3.5' only ever resolved to a preview build that has no ubuntu-26.04 binary.

Dependencies

  • Go module and GitHub Actions bumps (#907): golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0 (with x/sys v0.49.0, x/text v0.43.0, x/tools v0.51.0), urfave/cli/v3 v3.14.0, onsi/gomega v1.44.0, stretchr/testify v1.12.1, mattn/go-isatty v0.0.24 and github/codeql-action v4.39.1.

[v0.5.0] - 2026-10-13

Features

  • feat(aws): optional availabilityZone on instance and cluster specs (#878, @​abrarshivani): Pins every subnet and node to one zone of the region. The pre-flight rejects a pinned zone that does not offer the requested instance types and lists the zones that do.

Bug Fixes

  • fix(aws): create subnets in an availability zone that offers the instance types (#878, @​abrarshivani): Subnets were created without an Availability Zone, so AWS could place them in a zone that does not offer the instance type (for example g5g.xlarge in us-west-2d). RunInstances then failed after the VPC existed, and the rollback could leak the VPC. The pre-flight now uses DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings to pick a standard zone that offers every instance type the environment needs, and Create(), CreateCluster() and DryRun() fail before anything is created when no zone does. An identity without ec2:DescribeAvailabilityZones or ec2:DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings gets a warning and the previous behaviour, unless availabilityZone is set.
  • fix(release): open tap bumps as PRs from per-release branches (#884): GoReleaser now commits the Homebrew Formula and Cask bumps to brew/holodeck-formula-X.Y.Z and brew/holodeck-cask-X.Y.Z and opens a PR for each, instead of committing to main. HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN needs only Contents and Pull requests write access.

Security

  • golang.org/x/net bumped to v0.60.0 (#895): Fixes GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6612 and GO-2026-6617. The other golang.org/x modules move with it (crypto v0.57.0, sys v0.48.0, text v0.42.0).

Dependencies

New Contributors

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2's releases.

v2.34.0

Features

  • DeferOnFailure registers a callback that runs only when a spec fails - as soon as the failing node returns and before any teardown (JustAfterEach, AfterEach, AfterAll, DeferCleanup) - so it can capture the state teardown is about to destroy. It takes exactly what DeferCleanup takes and shares its scoping: called in BeforeEach/JustBeforeEach/It it covers the spec, in BeforeAll the ordered container, and in BeforeSuite the whole suite. It is also available on GinkgoT(); note that this adds a method to FullGinkgoTInterface, so hand-written implementations of that interface need to add it. See https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/#capturing-failure-state-deferonfailure

Fixes

  • Progress reporters (AttachProgressReporter) are no longer called while Ginkgo holds an internal lock, so a reporter that calls CurrentSpecReport() or AddReportEntry() no longer stalls for 5 seconds and has its output dropped.

title: Fix persistence daemon socket lookup in operand images
body: ## Description When CDI mounts the persistence daemon socket at `/run/nvidia-persistenced/socket`, NVML cannot find it at `/var/run/nvidia-persistenced/socket` because the device-plugin image has a separate `/var/run` directory. title: [Bug]: gpu-feature-discovery exits when a periodic label update hits a transient API error
body:
**Motivation**

We run GPU Feature Discovery on a large production fleet. Whenever nodes briefly lose contact with the API server, GFD pods across the fleet exit and restart at the same time.

- [x] I would like to work on this issue.

### 1. Quick Debug Information
* OS/Version(e.g. RHEL8.6, Ubuntu22.04): Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
* Kernel Version: 5.15.0-177-generic
* Container Runtime Type/Version(e.g. Containerd, CRI-O, Docker): containerd 1.7.28
* K8s Flavor/Version(e.g. K8s, OCP, Rancher, GKE, EKS): Kubernetes v1.34.8
* GFD v0.19.0 with the NodeFeature API enabled. The same code is in v0.20.0 and on `main`.

### 2. Issue or feature description

`run()` in `cmd/gpu-feature-discovery/main.go` regenerates labels every sleep interval. Any error from `d.labelOutputer.Output(labels)` is returned from `run()`, `start()` returns it, and the process exits with status 1. This happens on every periodic refresh, not only at startup. With the NodeFeature API, one failed request for the node's NodeFeature object is enough, for example during an API server restart or a short network interruption:

```
I1126 09:10:59.329594    1731 main.go:281] Creating Labels
I1126 09:11:02.267729    1731 main.go:160] Exiting
E1126 09:11:02.267751    1731 main.go:127] failed to get NodeFeature object: Get "https://<apiserver>:443/apis/nfd.k8s-sigs.io/v1alpha1/namespaces/gpu-operator/nodefeatures/nvidia-features-for-<node>": dial tcp <apiserver>:443: ...
```

Labels that were already applied stay in place, so the result is restart churn rather than lost labels. However, every GFD pod refreshes on the same interval, so a single API disruption restarts them across the fleet. On one cluster, 83 GFD pods had each restarted between 5 and 60 times with exit code 1, and their latest restarts cluster together: 19 pods within the same ten minutes one day, and 13 within ten minutes later that day. Pods that fail repeatedly also end up in CrashLoopBackOff.

**Expected behavior:** once labels have been written successfully, a failed periodic update is logged and retried at the next interval. Failing to write labels at startup can stay fatal.

**Current behavior:** any failed periodic update terminates the process.

### 3. Information to attach

The GFD container log excerpt above shows the failure.
